data.flag: High missing data (>20%) in: credit_limit, drawn_balance, ead_at_default, loan_term_years, default_date, ltv, recovery_rate
data.suggestion: Investigate the root cause of missingness (MAR/MCAR/MNAR). Apply appropriate imputation or exclude columns exceeding the 20% threshold. Document the data quality assessment and remediation steps per SS1/23 Principle 3.2.

training.flag: Cross-validation was not performed. SS1/23 Principle 3.3 requires backward-looking stability testing across multiple data samples — stratified K-Fold CV (k≥5) must be run and fold-level metrics reported to demonstrate model stability.
training.suggestion: Enable K-Fold cross-validation in the training step. Report mean and standard deviation of ROC-AUC, recall, and PR-AUC across folds in the validation report per SS1/23 Principle 3.3.

evaluation.flag: No sensitivity analysis has been performed. SS1/23 Principle 3.3 requires backward-looking and forward-looking sensitivity testing — the effect of parameter perturbations on model outputs must be documented.
evaluation.suggestion: Run a sensitivity analysis varying key model parameters (±10%, ±25%). Document how predictions change under adverse macro scenarios and include results in the model validation report.

evaluation.flag: Model explainability analysis (SHAP) was not performed. SS1/23 Principle 3.5 requires model inputs and their relative contributions to be documented and explainable to non-technical stakeholders and regulators. SS1/23 Principle 4.2 additionally requires that model outputs be explainable using model-agnostic interpretability techniques (e.g. SHAP, LIME) to support human oversight and credit decisions.
evaluation.suggestion: Run SHAP value analysis on Step 7 (Explainability). Produce a SHAP summary plot and document the top contributing features in the model card per SS1/23 Principles 3.5 and 4.2.
